note: Hand-written headers that SHADOW the generated tree. An override is placed earlier on the include path than the generated include directory, so the generated file stays untouched and the override is the whole of the modification: the set of files under overrides/include is the diff, and no computation is needed to find it. Reserved for what the declared mechanisms cannot reach -- source-patches/ rewrites the pinned TypeScript, repairs/ adds text with no behavior to emitted output, and either is preferable because neither carries a copy. An override does carry a copy, so each entry records `derivedFrom`, the sha256 of the generated file it was produced from. When a pin move changes that file the digest stops matching and `npm run overrides:check` says so, which is the signal to re-derive the override or drop it. Each entry also carries a `status`: `complete` means the override compiles, `incomplete` means it is partway and says what remains, so nobody mistakes a half-finished override for a finished one.

overrides.equivalence: Each cache is the source's own map: one per program lifetime, keyed by the context's identity (two copies of one context are one key), holding the context weakly; cached programs hold their surface only weakly, so no value keeps its key alive, and an expired entry is purged before the next lookup. overrides.whyNotAPatchOrRepair: A source patch re-spelling the key as WebGL2RenderingContext (the render-gl precedent) would still leave the dropped spread and the split carrier, which are emission defects; an emission repair may not add storage. overrides.reason: The 806d257 emission of spineParseHelpers.ts does not compile, so no consumer of the module (including clampUnit) can include it. After `Array.isArray` on an unknown value it reads `raw.length` / `curve.length` as `named_properties(x).get("length")`, which is an Any and has no length behind it, because `named_properties` only sees AnyObject owners. It indexes `curve[i]` with a subscript flight::Any does not have. It passes each diagnostic detail object literal as a bare braced pair list into the optional<Record> parameter (docs/compiler-requests/optional-record-literal-not-materialized.md). And it reads `keys[i].curve` with `.value()`, which throws for a keyframe that has no `curve`, where TypeScript reads undefined.
overrides.change:
Seven expressions differ from the generated 806d257 header; every other byte is the emission:
- The three erased length reads become `static_cast<double>(x.array_size())`.
- The four `curve[offset + k]` reads become `curve.array_get(offset + k).value_or(flight::Any(flight::undefined))`.
- The `curve` member read becomes `.value_or(flight::Any(flight::undefined))`.
- The three detail literals name `flight::Record<String, variant<bool, double, String>>{...}` inside the optional slot.
overrides.equivalence: `Any::array_size` and `Any::array_get` read the live original typed array storage without copying it, whatever element type it was boxed at, so the length and elements are the array's current ones, as JavaScript reads them. A missing, fractional or past-end index is absent, which `value_or(undefined)` turns into the undefined that `numberOr` maps to its fallback, as in the source. An absent `curve` member is undefined, so `Array.isArray` is false and the interval eases to null, as the source does instead of throwing. Each diagnostic detail Record holds the same single key and numeric value and is engaged in its optional, as the literal is. clampUnit, indexOfBone, indexOfSpineSlot, numberOr, parseSpineColor, the constants and every declaration are unchanged.
overrides.whyNotAPatchOrRepair: No faithful TypeScript spelling reads an erased array: each respelling measured in docs/compiler-requests/erased-array-element-reading.md is refused or fails to compile, and asserting the curve's element type would narrow its domain. An emission repair may only add behaviorless text, while these are changed expressions. The runtime half is the checked erased-array API (`Any::array_size` / `array_get`), which is now supplied.
overrides.unblocks: flight/skeleton2d_formats/spine_parse_helpers.hpp compiles, so clampUnit and the other Spine parse helpers are consumable through the original public header.
overrides.remaining: None in this module's emitted declarations or behavior. The `Array.isArray(unknown)` guard depends on the runtime's free `flight::is_array(const Any&)` (being added by builder4); without it the generic catch-all returns false for every boxed array.
overrides.expires: when the pinned compiler lowers erased array length/index reads through the checked Any array API, names the optional diagnostic Record, and reads an absent Record member as undefined for spineParseHelpers.ts.
